answer.rationale: Constraints eliminate most directions before evidence even matters. Rollback is off the table: compliance has ruled the security patch non-revertible, so memory_b1 and memory_b6 (both about release gating/reverting) are inapplicable however reliable they are. Circuit breaker (memory_b4) works by failing fast, which on a heavy write path at settlement peak means shedding exactly the customer writes the primary objective says not to lose. Regional failover (memory_b2) recovered a latency degradation, but that record is about latency recovery, not about write durability during a failover with in-flight settlement writes; shifting a write-heavy peak across regions risks replication gaps. Add capacity (memory_b3) worked as pre-provisioning ahead of a known promotional window; it does not transfer cleanly to a mid-incident intervention where provisioning lead time likely exceeds the remaining window of the 90-minute climb. That leaves read-replica routing, which is the only candidate that reduces load on the contended primary without rejecting or endangering writes. I am spending the single verification on memory_b5 because it is the one memory I actually intend to act on and its transferability is the crux: I need the original record to check whether the write-latency recovery came from read offload on a comparable write-heavy primary, or whether that incident was read-dominated and the mechanism will not reproduce here. Key uncertainty that verification may not resolve: I have not established that read contention is the cause of the current climb. If the driver is lock contention, checkpoint/IO saturation, or a regression in the new build's write path, offloading reads will help little, and the new build is a live suspect I cannot test by reverting. So this runs as a small guarded test: route reporting and dashboard reads only, incrementally, with replica lag and primary write p99 as the ramp gates, and stop if lag grows without write-latency improvement. Downstream value risk: replica reads are stale by construction, so any settlement reconciliation, balance display, or risk check that silently picks up replica data could propagate wrong figures into financial decisions downstream. Read routing must be scoped to reporting paths that tolerate staleness and explicitly excluded from reconciliation and authorization reads, with that boundary recorded for the next session.
